newsitem.title: UK: Kuwait sees oil glut persisting in Q2 1997.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait sees oil glut persisting in Q2 1997.

text.p: Kuwaiti Oil Minister Isa al-Mazeedi said on Tuesday he believed the current oil glut would continue into the second quarter of the year but higher demand for gasoline should keep prices steady.

Mazeedi, speaking in an interview with the London-based newspaper Asharq al-Awsat, also said he believed OPEC's decision to maintain a freeze on quotas could have contributed to the problem of cheating.
"By end 1996, oil prices averaged $21 a barrel but some oil products -- like gas oil and diesel -- began to retreat in early 1997," Mazeedi said.

"All indications are that the current production glut will continue in the second quarter of the year but because this period sees demand rising for light products...and the industry begins to build stocks, these factors should minimise the impact on prices," he added.

Mazeedi also said Kuwait would seek an increase in its OPEC quota of 2.0 million barrels per day (bpd) at the next OPEC ministerial meeting in June if the organisation decided to raise its ceiling from the current 25.03 million bpd.

"But the issue of raising the ceiling will depend on market conditions...Kuwait is keen to abide by all OPEC agreements except that sadly we have noticed that some members have been producing above quota. This has been detrimental to OPEC and members abiding by quotas," Mazeedi said.
"It might be that OPEC's decision to freeze quotas for such a long time has exacerbated the problem of overproduction by some members," he added.
OPEC has kept quotas frozen for all members but Iraq since September 1993 in a bid to prop up prices.
